Hi Maria / Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

Call summary
- Use case: internal triage assistant for patient intake forms (classification + suggested follow-ups).
- Concern: ensuring PHI/PII from prompts and model outputs are handled to meet HealthTech's compliance needs (data residency, retention, logging controls, ability to opt out of model training).

Ask I promised to follow up on: PII handling for prompts/outputs — specifically: what Redwood stores, where it is stored, and retention windows. See answers below (high-level) and attached FAQ + DPA for details.

High-level PII handling options (hosted API)
- Default (hosted): prompts and outputs are retained for short-term monitoring and abuse detection. Our standard retention window is up to 30 days by default for hosted customers; this helps with debugging, abuse monitoring, and quality checks.
- Opt-out / no-retention: For customers on a paid plan or via additional contractual terms, we support disabling prompt/output retention for production traffic (no prompts/outputs persist beyond ephemeral processing).
- Data residency: Hosted logs are stored in the region you select (US or EU) for customers who require data residency; we can surface region selection during onboarding and in Dedicated/Private deployments.

Dedicated / Private deployment options
- Dedicated: Reserved capacity where logs can be configured to not persist prompts/outputs; retention rules are set per-customer and can be zero depending on the contract.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Customer controls storage; Redwood’s control plane can operate in-region and logs/audit trails remain inside the customer VPC.

Logging, audit trails, and redaction
- Audit logs: We provide immutable audit logs for administrative actions; standard retention for audit metadata is 12 months (configurable via contract).
- Redaction: We support pre-processing redaction hooks and tokenization that can remove/replace PII fields before they are sent to the model. Neha (cc'd) can share examples of regex-based and form-field extraction flows we’ve implemented with other customers.

Next steps
1) I’ll attach the PII FAQ and a current DPA draft (attached).
2) Neha to propose a short PoC plan that demonstrates no-retention traffic and PII redaction in staging.
3) Maria / Tom to confirm whether HealthTech needs EU residency or US-only for this project and any minimum audit retention requirements.

If that looks right I’ll follow up with a proposed PoC schedule early next week.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra

2) For the "opt-out / no-retention" option, does Redwood still store metadata (request IDs, timestamp, model/route) for billing and rate-limiting? If yes, what fields persist and for how long?

Hi Maria — great questions. Short answers below; Neha is copied to add technical details and confirm PoC scope.

1) Retention mechanics: the 30-day default is automated rolling deletion — data older than the retention window is purged automatically from our hot logs. Backups/snapshots do not retain prompt text beyond the retention window for hosted customers; backups containing logs are encrypted and governed by our backup retention policy (we’ll include language in the DPA).

2) Metadata retention: when opting out of prompt/output retention we still maintain minimal telemetry for billing and performance (request ID, timestamp, model id/route, token counts). These fields do not contain user text or output. Default retention for telemetry is 12 months, but we can negotiate shorter windows in the contract for customers with stricter needs.

3) EU residency: yes — for hosted customers who request EU residency we confine storage of prompts/outputs and logs to the EU region and do not replicate raw prompt/output text to US systems. Note that certain control plane metadata used for multi-region routing may be aggregated in an anonymized/metadata-only form; we’ll surface precise mappings in the DPA.

PoC scope proposal (high level)
- PoC goal: demonstrate redaction pipeline + no-retention request path.
- Steps: (1) we'll provide a short JS webhook example that strips PHI fields before send; (2) deploy a no-retention route for your staging API key; (3) capture and show audit logs for admin access.
- Timeline: Neha can spin up the PoC environment in 3 business days once we have an NDA/DPA in place.

Neha — can you reply with the PoC checklist and an example pre-processing redaction snippet? I’ll attach the FAQ and current DPA to the portal for Maria / Tom.

Thanks —
Rishi

Hi Maria / team —

Quick PoC checklist and redaction snippet:

PoC checklist
- Provide staging API key with no-retention flag set.
- Example pre-processing layer (lambda) that redacts fields: name, phone, email, SSN, MRN.
- Deploy a test route that returns the model response but does not persist prompt/output to disk.
- Show admin audit logs (access timestamps + actor) for the PoC window (we’ll retain 6 months for audit metadata during PoC).

Redaction snippet (Python, illustrative):
- import re
- def redact(text):
-    text = re.sub(r" \d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4} ", "[SSN]", text)  # SSN example
-    text = re.sub(r"[\w\.-]+@[\w\.-]+", "[EMAIL]", text)
-    text = re.sub(r" \d{3}-\d{3}-\d{4} ", "[PHONE]", text)
-    return text

Notes
- The PoC will show the request flow end-to-end; no raw prompts will be written to persistent logs in the no-retention route. We will, however, keep minimal telemetry (request id, timestamp, model route) for debugging.
- For production, we recommend combining client-side redaction with server-side pre-processing for defense in depth.

I’ll follow up with a short PoC runbook and share a staging API key in a separate secure message.

Thanks,
